Lessons.Title: Locate Unit Fractions on the Number Line
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 original Warm-up, Which One Doesn't Belong: Fraction Details, shows four illustrations A–D: A shaded one-third of a three-part rectangle; B a zero-to-one number line with two interior marks; C a zero-to-one line with a point at one-third; D a zero-to-one line with quarter marks and the first point labeled one-fourth. Each can be distinguished by different mathematical features. Multiple justified answers are allowed; no unique choice is imposed.

2021 original Activity 1, Partition Fourths, shows Clare, Andre and Diego marking a number line extending from zero through one to two. Only Andre's approach partitions the UNIT interval 0-to-1 into FOUR equal parts. Clare divides the ENTIRE 0-to-2 line into four equal pieces, which makes each piece one-half of the 0-to-1 unit, not one-fourth. Diego places four tick marks between 0 and 1, which yields FIVE intervals, not fourths. Students must reason about why Andre makes the most sense, not mark all three as equivalent.

2021 original Activity 2, Unit Fractions on the Number Line, provides nine distinct subtasks in this exact fraction order: 1/4, 1/8, 1/3, 1/6, 1/2, then 1/4, 1/8, 1/3, 1/6. First four figures are single 0-to-1 units; subsequent source images display extended number lines 0-to-4, 0-to-2, 0-to-4, 0-to-3 and 0-to-2 respectively. Pupils partition the ZERO-TO-ONE UNIT equally into denominator-sized intervals and mark the requested FIRST unit-fraction point from zero, even if the full line extends beyond one whole.

For each original fraction question: 1/n sits one equal 0-to-1 interval after zero. If the displayed source line spans m wholes, then maintain the same unit scale across the entire line; for instance the line 0-to-4 containing 1/2 has its 1/2 point halfway between 0 and 1, NOT halfway from 0 to 4 (which is 2). Similarly 1/8 of one unit on a 0-to-4 line is not 4/8 or 1/2 of its total length.

The teacher's original discussion compares length 1 and length 2 number lines and prompts students to justify the unit anchor, spacing and meaning. Compare different correct constructions while preserving 0-to-1 as one, even when the complete number line is longer. Equal physical gaps and the reasoning for a mark are teacher-reviewed; numeric fraction identification alone cannot certify partition construction.

The source publisher Cool-down, Locate and Label, is not available as a public copy. The first-party Edulytics independent Cool-down may target the same mathematical goal but is neither the original prompt nor teacher-approved publisher parity; original source artwork is read for analysis but not embedded.

KeyConcepts.Title: One whole on a number line
KeyConcepts.Definition: Distance from 0 to 1 is the reference unit regardless of how far the number line continues.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Divide the interval 0-to-1 into n EQUAL spaces to locate 1/n.
KeyConcepts.Example: First point after zero in 4 equal unit intervals is 1/4.

KeyConcepts.Title: Marks versus spaces
KeyConcepts.Definition: An interior tick divides a space; count consecutive spaces, not just marks.
KeyConcepts.Rule: k interior ticks between 0 and 1 make k+1 gaps.
KeyConcepts.Example: 3 inner ticks => 4 fourths; 4 inner ticks => 5 fifths.

KeyConcepts.Title: Extended whole-number lines
KeyConcepts.Definition: A line 0-to-4 displays four whole units, not one.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Mark 1/n relative to first one-unit interval even if rightmost endpoint is 2,3,4.
KeyConcepts.Example: 1/2 on 0-to-4 is between 0 and 1, not at 2.

KeyConcepts.Title: Compare student strategies
KeyConcepts.Definition: Analyze correctness of partition relative to the unit reference.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Clare divides the whole 0-to-2 into four; Diego counts ticks; Andre quarters 0-to-1.

WorkedExamples.Title: Partition fourths, not half-units
WorkedExamples.Question: Why is Andre's number line more accurate than Clare's and Diego's?
WorkedExamples.Method: Identify the one-unit interval and count equal spaces.
Steps: A whole on a number line runs from 0 to 1.
Clare divides 0-to-2 into four equal gaps of length 1/2 each.
Diego puts four interior marks in 0-to-1, which makes five gaps.
Andre divides 0-to-1 into four equal gaps; first gap ends at 1/4.
WorkedExamples.Check: Four equal 1/4 gaps make one whole.

WorkedExamples.Title: Locate 1/4 on 0-to-1
WorkedExamples.Question: Partition zero to one to locate 1/4.
Steps: Draw three equally spaced interior marks.

WorkedExamples.Title: Locate 1/8 on 0-to-1
WorkedExamples.Question: Locate 1/8.
WorkedExamples.Method: Divide unit into eight equal gaps.
Steps: Place seven equal interior marks in 0-to-1.

WorkedExamples.Title: Locate 1/3 on 0-to-1
WorkedExamples.Question: Locate 1/3.
WorkedExamples.Method: Divide unit into three equal gaps.
Steps: Split zero to one into three equal distances.

WorkedExamples.Title: Locate 1/6 on 0-to-1
WorkedExamples.Question: Locate 1/6.
WorkedExamples.Method: Divide unit into six equal gaps.
Steps: Mark five equally spaced interior points.

WorkedExamples.Title: Extended 0-to-4 line, 1/2
WorkedExamples.Question: Find 1/2 on a number line whose rightmost mark is 4.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the interval from 0 to 1 as one whole.
Steps: Divide ONLY the first unit 0-to-1 into two equal spaces.
Label midpoint 1/2; the midpoint of 0-to-4 is 2, not 1/2.
WorkedExamples.Check: 1/2 lies between zero and one even on a multi-whole line.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Count four interior marks as four equal intervals.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Four interior marks create five gaps.
CommonMistakes.Correction: For fourths put exactly three interior marks in 0-to-1.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Split an entire 0-to-2 line into four and call each length one fourth.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Each span is one-half of the 0-to-1 whole.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Anchor one whole to 0..1 before partitioning.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Put 1/2 at the center of a 0-to-4 line.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: That center is the number 2; 1/2 is halfway from zero to one.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Match fractional coordinates to the unit reference.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claim all students' fourths approaches are valid.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Clare and Diego commit different original 2021 source misconceptions.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Choose Andre and explain errors specifically, not merely whose picture looks better.

SummaryPoints: Warm-up A–D has multiple defensible one-doesn't-belong classifications; teacher checks rationale.
Partition Fourths comparison: Andre is correct; Clare divides TWO wholes into four; Diego counts FOUR tick marks but makes FIVE gaps.
The exact nine Activity 2 source targets are 1/4,1/8,1/3,1/6,1/2,1/4,1/8,1/3,1/6.
The later five source number lines extend beyond 1, but the denominator partitions the 0-to-1 UNIT.
Original 22 source-image instances were read on device (repeated source files deduplicated by SHA). Reproduction, full publisher student PDF and Stage D are not certified.
